packs.title: Buttons Together (Co-Op GAME for 1-6)
packs.short: Every button has a purpose, every room hides a challenge, and your friends might be your only way out.
packs.descriptionHtml:
**Every room has a door. Somewhere on the walls is the button that opens it. Everything else? Well… press it and find out.**

Buttons Together is a co-op escape game for 1–6 players. Climb 100 rooms with your friends, read what each button does, solve circuits and puzzles together, and try not to set off the alarm by mashing everything in sight.

### How it works

- **100 rooms, 10 floors.** Room 100's door is the way out. Your escape time is saved, so try to beat it.

- **Shared team lives.** The team has 3 lives. If everyone goes down at once, you lose one and restart the room. Each new floor gives one back.

- **Every button does something.** Food, water, glasses, medkits, toys, rifles, fake monsters, earthquakes… One of them is the door.

- **Press with care.** From room 41, panic-pressing sets off the alarm. The door locks, everyone gets shocked, and searchlights, spikes and poison gas show up.

### The journey

- **Rooms 1–20, Learning:** buttons, items and finding the door. It ends at the **shooting range** in room 20.

- **Rooms 21–40, Door circuits:** pressing the door button isn't enough anymore. Watch which buttons light up, memorise light sequences, solve linked switches and press together on time. Every room is a different scenario.

- **Rooms 41–60, Room games and the alarm:** room timers, a noise meter and a new floor game in each room.

- **Rooms 61–80, Mixed rooms:** circuits, games and the alarm all at once.

- **Rooms 81–100, Logic track and finale:** locks, math, patterns, clocks, logic, jigsaws, mazes, lasers and sudoku. Then the celebration room.

### Things that want you gone

Drifting shadows, sweeping searchlights, creatures crawling out of the vents with ground slams and rings of fire, and floor wardens at the end of every floor. Stay quiet, stay together, and pick each other up.

### The announcer

A soft, robotic train-station voice follows you through every room. It explains the rules, comforts you after a bad fall, and won't let your hat choice go unremarked. More than 200 voiced lines in English and Turkish, with subtitles in 6 languages.

### And also

- Customise your character with hats and outfits.

- An end-of-run team report card: Door Hunter, Puzzle Genius, Lifesaver, Alarm Enthusiast, Never Gets Up…

- Play solo, over Steam with friends (no port forwarding needed) or over LAN.

### Requirements

- Windows 10/11, 64-bit, a DirectX 12 graphics card

- For online play, Steam must be running and you must be signed in

- Everyone in a session must use the same version

**Languages:** Voice in English and Turkish · Subtitles in English, Turkish, German, French, Spanish and Russian

packs.title: Say or Boom: A Hilarious Bomb Timer Game!
packs.descriptionHtml:
Game Overview:

Think fast and have a blast with Think Fast, Pass Faster! This high-energy game will test your reflexes and quick thinking as you race against the bomb timer. Gather your friends, sit in a circle, and be ready for some quick action. The game revolves around naming examples related to a place or type (like “hospital” or “zoo”) before the timer runs out. If you explode 3 times, you’re out of the game!

How to Play:

  • Sit in a circle with your friends and get ready to pass the phone.
  • One player starts by showing a place or type picture (like “beach”).
  • The next player must give a related example (like “lifeguard”) and pass the phone quickly.
  • Keep passing the phone clockwise, making sure to come up with new examples before the bomb goes off.
  • If the bomb explodes while you’re holding the phone, you get a strike! Three strikes, and you're out of the game.

Bomb Timer:

  • The ticking bomb adds suspense and excitement to each round. You never know when it’ll go off!

Game Rules:

  • Pass the phone clockwise after giving your example.
  • No repeating examples—once something is said, it’s out of play.
  • Don’t take too long to answer, or the bomb might explode in your hands!
  • No hard feelings, and don’t blame the person who gave you the phone!

Objective: Be the last one standing! Keep your wits sharp and your answers quicker than the ticking timer to survive the game.

This game is all about fun, fast-paced action, and keeping the pressure on. Are you ready to outthink the bomb?

Cooked Card Deck — 5 Themes

A complete playing card deck in five themes that match our Softline UI Kit: Soft Glass, Cozy Chunky, Clean Paper, Flat Night (vector) and a hand-drawn Pixel theme.

What's inside (every theme, same 63 files)

  • 52 cards (A, 2-10, J, Q, K in hearts, diamonds, clubs and spades), four-colour suits for easy reading
  • 2 jokers
  • 2 card backs; both look the same either way up, so they never give away how a card was dealt
  • Blank face, selection glow and an empty pile slot

  • Vector themes: SVG + PNG at 1x and 2x. Pixel theme: native pixels, x4 and x8

Made for solitaire, poker, blackjack, card battlers and any game that needs a clean, readable deck. A Unity package with a demo scene is on our Unity Asset Store page.

Side view and top-down: 49 effects come in a side and a top-down version: the ones where gravity or ground contact matters (explosions with debris, landings, ground spells, breaking props). The side version is for platformers: things arc, fall and land on the ground line. The top-down version is for top-down games: things spread out over the floor. The other 201 effects have a single version that is not tied to a camera angle (projectiles, auras, flashes, pickups, UI).

Colour tones: 81 effects also come in extra colour tones (2 to 5 colours each), for example laser beam in red, green, blue and purple, or blood burst in red, green and purple.

Loops and one-shots: 74 seamless loops and 176 one-shots. The one-shots are built in clear beats: a short build-up, the hit, follow-through and a fade-out.

Format

  • PNG sprite sheets with a transparent background, one sheet per animation, frames left to right in square cells. The PNGs use an 8-bit palette with full transparency (colour-reduced to keep the download small)
  • 24 fps: one-shots of 16 to 32 frames and loops of 24 to 48 frames
  • Three cell sizes, picked by how much room an effect needs: 174 effects use the 128 px cell, 47 the 192 px cell and 29 the 256 px cell. The scale is the same in all three, so effects from different cells fit together
  • Every sheet at 1x (folder PNG_1x) and at 2x (PNG_2x; 2x cells: 256, 384 and 512 px). PNG only, no SVG files
  • Sheets are single rows, so long animations are wide: up to 9216 px at 1x and 18432 px at 2x. Check your engine's maximum texture size (in Unity, raise Max Size in the import settings; the default is 2048). 7 of the 2x sheets are wider than 16384 px, a common graphics card limit: use the 1x sheet for those
  • anims.json: frames, fps, cell size, loop, view, facing and pivot of every sheet. The pivot is the ground line for side-view effects and the cell centre for the others
  • index.csv: the same list as a table that opens in any spreadsheet
  • 74 directional effects face right (projectiles, slashes, beams, dashes): flip or rotate them in your engine
  • README.pdf and LICENSE.pdf

Works in any engine that can play a sprite sheet: Godot, Unity, GameMaker, Unreal, Construct, Phaser or your own. The download is art and data only: PNG files, anims.json and index.csv (the same list as a table), with no engine plug-in or scripts to install. Slice each sheet by its cell size and play it at its fps; both are listed in anims.json.

Part of the Softline family

Colours, outlines and shadows use the Softline UI Kit tokens, so the effects sit naturally next to Softline UI Kit - Clean Paper and the Clean Paper theme of Softline UI Kit - Cards and Softline UI Kit - Bars.

They are built with the same drawing engine and palette as our free Cooked FX (40 effects). None of those 40 is reused here: all 250 are newly drawn, also where they cover the same moment (a slash, a muzzle flash, a landing). Together with the free Cooked FX Environment & Emotes (40 more) that is 330 effects that mix in one game.

Not sure which theme fits your game? Both free packs contain all five themes, so you can try Clean Paper in your project first.

Other editions (the same 250 effects in another theme): Cooked FX 250 - Soft Glass, Cooked FX 250 - Cozy Chunky, Cooked FX 250 - Flat Night, Cooked FX 250 - Pixel.

Softline UI Sounds - Clean Paper is a set of 100 game UI sound effects (204 files) in the Clean Paper theme of our Softline family. Clean Paper is the dry, close desk sound: paper flicks, page turns, pencil taps, check-mark scratches and rubber stamps, with a soft plucked tone only for successes and rewards. It is paper-style synthesis, not recorded paper foley. Key of C major.

It is made to match the Clean Paper theme of Softline UI Kit and Softline UI Screens (sold separately), so your menus look and sound like one set. Every sound is measured and balanced, so the whole pack plays well at one volume.

Listen first: the sound board on this page plays all 204 files in your browser (preview quality).

100 sounds in 10 groups

  • Buttons (7 sounds, 15 files): button hover, button click, button press, button release, button disabled, hold fill loop, hold complete
  • Controls (15 sounds, 31 files): toggle on, toggle off, checkbox on, checkbox off, radio select, slider tick, slider grab, slider release, slider limit, stepper up, stepper down, tab switch, dropdown open, dropdown close, scroll tick
  • Navigation and windows (12 sounds, 26 files): menu move, menu select, menu back, window open, window close, popup open, popup close, panel in, panel out, tooltip show, page next, page prev
  • Feedback and alerts (11 sounds, 26 files): confirm, cancel, error, warning, notification, message in, message out, success, fail, saved, locked
  • Text and dialogue (9 sounds, 23 files): text blip low, text blip mid, text blip high, type key, type backspace, type submit, dialog open, dialog next, dialog close
  • Economy and rewards (16 sounds, 29 files): coin, coins many, gem, purchase, not enough, reward small, reward big, reward reveal, unlock, level up, achievement, star 1, star 2, star 3, counter loop, counter end
  • Inventory and drag (10 sounds, 21 files): item pickup, item equip, item unequip, item drop, item use, drag start, drag drop, drag cancel, slot swap, craft complete
  • Timers and loading (7 sounds, 12 files): timer tick, timer urgent, countdown beep, countdown go, time up, loading loop, loading done
  • Transitions (6 sounds, 12 files): whoosh in, whoosh out, swipe, scene transition, riser, reveal hit
  • Stingers (7 sounds, 9 files): game start, pause, resume, victory, defeat, game over, new record

The sounds you hear most often (hovers, clicks, ticks, text blips, coins, menu moves) come in 2 to 4 variants, so repeats never sound the same.

Formats

  • WAV/ 48 kHz, 24-bit, mono: 204 files in 10 group folders (11.1 MB)
  • OGG/ an OGG Vorbis copy of every file, same folders and names (1.3 MB)
  • sounds.csv one row per file: group, sound, variant, file, loop, use, duration and measured loudness

Drop in, switch themes

Every file is named cleanpaper_sound_NN, for example cleanpaper_button_click_02.wav. All Softline UI Sounds themes use the same 100 sound names, group folders and variant numbers, each with its own prefix, so a game changes its whole sound by changing one prefix (or the folder).

Loudness and loops

  • Six loudness tiers, from -21 LUFS (hovers, ticks, typing) to -14 LUFS (coins, rewards, stingers), measured as the loudest moment (LUFS-M max). Frequent small sounds sit low, rare rewarding ones high.
  • True peak -1.0 dBTP or lower, no clipping, clean starts and ends without clicks or silence padding.
  • 4 seamless loop files (hold fill loop, counter loop, loading loop): no fades, no seam, just set them to loop.

Good to know

  • Lengths from 20 ms to 2.4 s. Works in any engine that plays WAV or OGG: Godot, Unity, Unreal, GameMaker, the web.
  • One theme per pack. README.pdf and LICENSE.pdf are included.

Other themes (the same 100 sounds in another style): Softline UI Sounds - Soft Glass, Softline UI Sounds - Cozy Chunky, Softline UI Sounds - Flat Night, Softline UI Sounds - Pixel.

The code uses NumPy / SciPy signal processing only (noise-based, paper-style synthesis, not recorded paper foley). No recorded samples and no AI audio-generation models were used. Every sound was measured and approved by ear by The Cooked Works. The page text was drafted with Claude's help.
